title: Unified API Gateway and Client SDK Layer
summary: Provide one secure, versioned, contract-first interface for AGASTYA web, CLI, SDK and approved integration clients.

intent.statement: Expose AGASTYA capabilities through one policy-enforced, project-scoped, contract-versioned API and matching client SDKs.
desired_outcomes: Every client request is authenticated, scoped, validated and auditable.
Clients use compatible typed contracts rather than internal implementation APIs.
Async engineering work reports truthful durable operation state.

success_measures.name: API contract coverage
success_measures.target: 100% supported gateway endpoints are represented by OpenAPI schemas and contract tests
success_measures.measurement_method: Compare registered endpoints with published contract and release test reports.

success_measures.name: Project-isolation enforcement
success_measures.target: 0 cross-project authorised reads/writes in security suite
success_measures.measurement_method: Execute cross-project and ambiguous-context negative tests.

problem.statement: Without a common API boundary, platform clients and integrations can bypass consistent project authorisation, validation, idempotency, evidence and compatibility controls.
problem.current_state: AGASTYA specifications define core domain capabilities but no unified client-facing contract, API policy layer or SDK release model.
impact: Client implementations could diverge from platform policy.
Breaking changes could disrupt tools and automation.
Long-running operations could be misrepresented as synchronous completion.

business_context.business_value: A stable gateway and generated SDKs make AGASTYA composable without widening security or eroding traceability.

stakeholders.name: Platform Engineering
stakeholders.role: Owns API contracts and gateway operations

stakeholders.name: Security Engineering
stakeholders.role: Owns identity, scopes and API controls

actors.name: Authenticated Human Client
goals: Read or command authorised project resources.

actors.name: Unified API Gateway
goals: Authenticate, authorise, validate, rate-limit and route requests.

functional_requirements.title: Publish canonical API contract
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall publish a canonical OpenAPI contract for all supported /api/v1 resources and commands, including schemas, scope, errors, examples and SDK metadata.

functional_requirements.title: Enforce client and project authorisation
functional_requirements.statement: The gateway shall authenticate clients, resolve exact tenant/project context and enforce server-side role/capability policy before every query or command.

functional_requirements.title: Validate schemas and safe errors
functional_requirements.statement: The gateway shall validate request and response schema, content type, size, classification and safe error behaviour for every endpoint.

functional_requirements.title: Support idempotency and concurrency
functional_requirements.statement: The gateway shall enforce idempotency for applicable commands and optimistic concurrency for versioned resource updates.

provenance.rationale: Safe retry and concurrent change handling.

functional_requirements.title: Expose durable operation resources
functional_requirements.statement: The gateway shall expose long-running work as durable Operation resources rather than holding synchronous requests open.

functional_requirements.title: Apply rate quota and evidence policy
functional_requirements.statement: The gateway shall apply project/client rate, concurrency and quota controls and append metadata-only audit/evidence events for material commands and access denials.

functional_requirements.title: Publish compatible client SDKs
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall generate or contract-test supported TypeScript and Python SDKs with injected auth providers, typed errors, cursor support and compatibility metadata.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Gateway and SDKs shall not expose secret plaintext, encrypted secret material, private reasoning, internal stacks or cross-project resource metadata.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Security suite tests error, response, SDK and cross-project denial surfaces.
non_functional_requirements.target: Zero sensitive disclosure in approved fixtures.

non_functional_requirements.statement: A retry using the same valid idempotency key shall not create duplicate material command outcomes.
non_functional_requirements.verification_method: Integration tests repeat commands under simulated client timeout and network retry.
non_functional_requirements.target: One committed command outcome per key/scope/request hash.

business_rules.statement: Every API request must resolve exactly one authorised tenant/project scope before resource data or command execution occurs.
A mutating command subject to retry/reordering requires a valid Idempotency-Key, and a versioned update requires current ETag or revision precondition.

constraints.statement: Initial public API uses OpenAPI-described REST under /api/v1; GraphQL, unauthenticated endpoints, direct internal service exposure and arbitrary webhook subscriptions are excluded.
constraints.rationale: A narrow contract-first boundary reduces attack surface and compatibility ambiguity.

dependencies.name: Identity and workload credential provider
dependencies.risk: Token, service identity and trust configuration require security architecture decision.

bounded_contexts.name: Platform API
bounded_contexts.responsibility: Own public API contracts, gateway policy, idempotency, operation representation, SDK release and client evidence.

ubiquitous_language.definition: Durable truthful representation of accepted asynchronous platform work.
Request key bound to principal, project, endpoint and normalised command hash.
Versioned published client agreement defining resources, schemas, security and errors.

workflows.name: Execute project-scoped asynchronous command
workflows.trigger: Authenticated client submits a valid v1 command.

steps.action: Authenticates client and resolves exact project/capability scope.
steps.result: Unauthorised or ambiguous request is denied.

steps.action: Validates schema, idempotency/precondition, rate/quota and policy.
steps.result: Command is rejected or accepted with correlation context.

steps.action: Creates durable Operation and returns safe typed response.
steps.result: Client observes truthful lifecycle/evidence without request blocking.

workflows.error_handling: Safe problem response includes correlation ID and retryability but no sensitive/internal fields.

security_requirements.statement: Gateway shall enforce authenticated, project-scoped server-side authorisation and safe classification/redaction for each API request and response.
security_requirements.verification_method: Negative security tests cover wrong-project query, stale token, excessive scope, malformed input and error disclosure.

observability_requirements.statement: Gateway shall emit correlation-linked request, policy, command, error, rate/quota and operation events without unsafe payloads.
observability_requirements.verification_method: End-to-end request trace reconstructs gateway decision and operation lifecycle through Ledger evidence.

acceptance_criteria.title: Contract and SDK are compatible
acceptance_criteria.given: A documented v1 endpoint and generated client method.
acceptance_criteria.then: OpenAPI schemas, examples and typed models remain compatible.

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-project request is denied
acceptance_criteria.given: A valid client without membership in target project.
acceptance_criteria.when: It reads or commands project resource.

acceptance_criteria.title: Idempotent retry commits once
acceptance_criteria.given: A valid mutation is repeated with same idempotency key.
acceptance_criteria.then: One result commits and stable prior status/response returns.

acceptance_criteria.title: Stale update conflicts safely
acceptance_criteria.given: Stale and current ETag update requests.
acceptance_criteria.then: Current update succeeds and stale update conflicts safely.

acceptance_criteria.title: Long-running work returns operation
acceptance_criteria.given: Command launches agent, verification or tool work.
acceptance_criteria.then: It returns 202 operation resource with truthful durable state.

acceptance_criteria.title: Quota limit is safe
acceptance_criteria.then: Gateway returns consistent limited outcome with no partial command.

acceptance_criteria.title: Unsafe input is rejected
acceptance_criteria.then: It rejects safely and excludes unsafe raw content from telemetry.

acceptance_criteria.title: Deprecation remains explicit
acceptance_criteria.then: Safe notice, compatibility policy and migration evidence exist.

test_requirements.scope: OpenAPI lint, examples, SDK generation and compatibility/deprecation checks.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Versioned contract and SDK release report.

test_requirements.scope: Authentication, project scope, schema, classification and safe-error negative suite.
test_requirements.expected_evidence: Denied requests and safe correlated audit records.

test_requirements.scope: Operation resource creation and truthful lifecycle projection.

test_requirements.expected_evidence: Limited request outcomes without partial command evidence.

risks.title: Gateway becomes bypassed or inconsistent policy point
risks.description: Internal services or SDKs could bypass central controls.
risks.mitigation: Publish only supported gateway interfaces, contract-test SDKs and deny internal capability exposure through public routes.

open_questions.question: Which identity provider, token format and service-workload credential model serve initial deployment?
open_questions.impact_if_unresolved: Gateway authentication and service client model cannot be finalised.
open_questions.resolution: Accepted as a detailed-design risk. Identity, token and workload credential architecture is mandatory before gateway deployment.

open_questions.question: Which gateway/runtime deployment topology meets rate, quota and operation event-stream SLOs?
open_questions.impact_if_unresolved: Gateway deployment/operational implementation cannot be selected.
open_questions.resolution: Accepted as a detailed-design risk. Gateway topology and SLO ADR are mandatory before deployment.

architecture_decisions.title: Use contract-first REST gateway with generated/verified SDKs
architecture_decisions.context: AGASTYA requires a stable external interface without exposing internal implementation surfaces or bypassing policy.
architecture_decisions.decision: Publish OpenAPI-described REST under /api/v1 with central gateway enforcement and TypeScript/Python SDKs generated from or contract-tested against the canonical contract.

alternatives.name: Direct internal service APIs
alternatives.rejection_reason: Creates inconsistent auth, versioning, audit and compatibility controls.

alternatives.name: GraphQL first
alternatives.rejection_reason: Increases initial policy/complexity surface before stable resource contracts exist.

architecture_decisions.rationale: One versioned resource/command boundary unifies governance and client experience.
consequences: Identity/gateway topology decisions remain mandatory before deployment.

provenance.rationale: Gateway must preserve project isolation and least privilege.

coverage_summary.method: Initial API gateway draft mapping; implementation coverage is not yet applicable.

change_history.reason: Define external contract/policy boundary before implementing public clients or SDKs.
